union_variant_offset_field_hazard.recorded_at_request_of: captain (t5 立案, t8 撑大检测门禁)
union_variant_offset_field_hazard.authoritative_rule: member offset MUST be taken from the KEY encoding (base before the underscore); never read a member-level offset field for union-variant members

MEASURED_FACTS_FROM_RAW_JSON.critical_correction_to_captains_premise: The captain described the field as a malformed 'base+index' string concatenation with values 121 / 16840 / 508140. On disk this is NOT the case: none of those three literals occurs anywhere in the respective JSON files (verified by grep: 16840 absent from RoleSystem.json, 508140 absent from SceneMgr.json, 121 absent from tagNewItem.json). More importantly, NONE of the 4 variant-key members has a member-level `offset` field at all - the field is absent, not malformed. The 10x values (121/16840/508140) are exactly base*10+index i.e. they are produced by CONCATENATING the key, so they are artifacts of a 10x reading, not stored data.
MEASURED_FACTS_FROM_RAW_JSON.nested_offset_fields_do_exist: Inline union/struct TYPES carry their own nested `offset` fields (e.g. RoleSystem.m_teamSlotOverlay's struct variant has m_fCBTimer offset=4 ... m_CCBStageCamBuffer offset=872). Those are offsets RELATIVE TO THE VARIANT START, which is a different semantic from the top-level member offset - a second, genuine way for a consumer to read a wrong number.

real_hazard_for_consumers: A consumer that does `m.get('offset')` on a variant-key member gets None (offset field absent). Depending on implementation it then places the member at 0, skips it, or raises - all wrong.
A consumer that reads nested type offsets as if they were top-level member offsets gets a wrong-relative value (relative-to-variant vs relative-to-struct).
A consumer that tries to reconstruct an offset by concatenating key and variant index gets a 10x-inflated value (this is precisely how the 121/16840/508140 artifacts arose).
